candidates.tagline: $2.2B stadium, glass railing in your sightline — architect says it's a feature
candidates.story: Buffalo's new $2.2B Highmark Stadium opened in August 2026 with glass safety railings that obstruct at least three rows of 400-level seats, and when fans complained the architect explained the blockage was an intentional consequence of concourse design decisions.
candidates.why_funny: Paying hundreds of dollars for an NFL seat only to be told the railing blocking your view was deliberately put there is architectural gaslighting at stadium scale.
candidates.alt: Interior of the new Highmark Stadium showing upper-level seating with glass safety railings partially blocking the sightline to the field below

candidates.tagline: No steering wheel, no pedals, no proven self-driving — launch is tomorrow
candidates.story: Tesla's Cybercab robotaxi officially launches September 3, 2026 — a two-seat car physically incapable of being driven by a human (no wheel, no pedals) whose only function depends on an autonomous system that has logged 380,000 driverless miles versus Waymo's 220 million.
candidates.why_funny: Mass-producing a car that cannot be operated without software that hasn't been proven to work is putting the robot before the robotaxi — Tesla is shipping 100+ units of a vehicle it 'can neither sell nor drive itself,' per Electrek.
candidates.alt: The Tesla Cybercab, a low-slung futuristic two-seat electric vehicle with butterfly doors and a minimalist interior — no steering wheel visible
